finding.claim: The host allowlist check uses `host.endswith("example.com")` with no leading dot. The `ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com"` constant is defined but never used. Any attacker-registered domain ending in `example.com` (for example `evilexample.com` or `attackerexample.com`) passes the check. The server then fetches the original unmodified URL. The attacker can point such a domain's DNS at an internal address (127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, RFC1918 hosts). DNS rebinding also works, because the check is hostname-only and runs before resolution. The response length is returned, which gives a content-length oracle and enables internal port and host scanning. Two parsers are also involved: `urlparse` validates and httpx fetches. That parser differential is a secondary risk, for example with backslash or userinfo forms.
finding.source: The `url` query parameter of GET /mirror (mirror.py:11), fully attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: `httpx.AsyncClient().get(url)` at mirror.py:16, called with the original unmodified URL string.

trace.note: `url: str` is read from the query string
`urlparse(url).hostname` is extracted, defaulting to an empty string

Only `host.endswith("example.com")` is checked. There is no dot boundary, no exact-match or allowlist, no scheme check, and no resolved-IP check. The unused ALLOWED_SUFFIX would have been the correct form.
httpx fetches the raw `url`. A host such as `evilexample.com` resolving to an internal IP is requested.
`len(r.text)` is returned to the attacker, giving a limited response oracle.

finding.guards_checked: Checked the suffix check at line 13. It is bypassable because it has no leading dot, so `evilexample.com` passes. It is a pre-DNS hostname-string check, so it is rebindable. It does not restrict the scheme, though httpx only supports http and https. It does not block private IPs or resolve addresses. Redirects: httpx's AsyncClient defaults to follow_redirects=False, so redirect-based bypass is not an additional vector. The /ping endpoint (line 20) uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a bare endswith("example.com") suffix check at mirror.py:13, which does not close the finding)
verdict.reason: The `url` query param (mirror.py:11) is attacker-controlled and reaches `c.get(url)` (mirror.py:16) guarded only by `host.endswith("example.com")` (mirror.py:13), so `evilexample.com` passes and the unused ALLOWED_SUFFIX (mirror.py:7) is never applied.
